spec_match.rationale: A genuine ::scroll-marker/::scroll-marker-group carousel whose one property is rewritten through every mode form the propdef names, with the cascade-fallback branch demonstrating exactly how an unsupported mode keyword degrades; mode meanings quoted from §3.1.6/§3.1.9.

interactive.rationale: Seven-way radio mode switch with live parsed/computed/pseudo-display readouts, real scroll-snap carousel with browser-generated markers, prev/next controls, live position readout, and a focus journal recording real focusin events.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a working carousel with a declaration toggle and live computed-value readback showing fallback — delivered verbatim.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the rejected-value cascade fallback (bare tabs on 141 observably falls back to 'after' / computed 'after links'), scroll-marker-group: none removing the group, the UA contain:size height trap (documented in the CSS comment), and browser-dependent pseudo-element focus reporting is disclosed rather than papered over.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5109685301673984, the §3.1.6 spec anchor, the v135 base-feature demo (avoiding duplicate coverage), and both sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's computed-round-trip and per-form css-supports assertions are the same contracts this page's readouts exercise, including the negative branches.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP-driven on headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37: 'after' → parsed yes / computed 'after links'; 'after tabs' → computed 'after tabs'; bare 'tabs' → parsed no / computed falls back to 'after links'; 'none' → computed 'none'; next-slide → 'Slide 2 of 5 in view'; ::scroll-marker-group resolves display:flex height:64px (no overlap after the contain:size fix); DevTools AX tree shows tablist + five selectable tab children in both modes, recorded in the page copy as the measured 141 state; zero console errors.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts carousel-init (base-marker and mode-keyword support), every mode-applied transition with parse/computed results, and carousel-scrolled with the slide index.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout including marker styling, page-local buttons and markers set background and color together, :target-current uses the black-on-ivory inversion, focus-visible outlines use accent-blue.

accessibility.rationale: Controls are native, labelled, 44px, keyboard-operable with aria-live readouts, and the AX tree was inspected (marker group exposes tablist/tab with selected state on 141); partial because the markers themselves are browser-generated pseudo-elements whose keyboard focusability cannot be guaranteed or remediated from the page across engines — the page discloses this and hands non-marker users the prev/next buttons.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 1280×2200 (screenshot read: carousel, markers, controls all visible and unclipped) and CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 touch: scrollWidth 360, no horizontal overflow, swipeable scroller, 44px radios/buttons/markers.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify activation focus and roving tabindex on a real Chrome 154 build
openQuestions.detail: On Chromium 141 the mode keywords parse but the AX mapping stays tablist/tab in both modes, so the focus-order differences §3.1.9 describes could not be observed natively. When a 154 or flag-enabled build is available, drive Tab/arrow keys through the real marker group in both modes, confirm the journal shows one stop (tabs) vs five (links), and confirm the links-mode AX tree flips to navigation/link.

openQuestions.title: Consider a many-slides variant to show tabs-mode value at scale
openQuestions.detail: The spec's motivating case is the 20-dot carousel tab trap. A variant with ~20 generated markers would make the links-vs-tabs stop-count difference dramatic once 154 semantics are live; today it would only differ in the hand-built reference page, so it was deferred with that reason rather than built as a near-duplicate.

guidanceConsulted.query: CSS carousel scroll markers accessible tabs pattern
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use scroll-snap with browser-derived active state instead of JS scroll listeners for highlighting; respect prefers-reduced-motion for snap effects.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Carousel uses scroll-snap-type x mandatory with :target-current for active-marker state (no JS state sync); the only motion added is user-initiated smooth scrollTo on the prev/next buttons, and no autonomous animation runs.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible tablist roving tabindex arrow key keyboard interaction
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Verify custom/generated semantics with the browser's accessibility-tree inspector rather than assuming markup implies exposure.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied literally: the DevTools protocol AX tree was captured in both modes and the measured tablist/tab exposure on 141 is quoted in the page's banner instead of an assumed links/tabs split.

summary: The carousel is real (Chrome 135 substrate) and the 154 delta is made observable twice over: the parse split via live parsed/computed readouts with an honest cascade fallback, and the semantics gap via a quoted AX-tree measurement showing tablist/tab in both modes on 141 — including the migration consequence that undeclared marker groups become navigation/link when 154 makes links the default.
